overall_reason: The job is reading and applying a reference list of interface rules (Read mode): one column at a readable measure on a 360px edge, category heads (Interactions, Animations, Layout, Content, Forms, Performance, Design) over bold-lead rules, then a Vercel-specific part and an agent-integration part, which is the structure the material needs.

score.reason: T-HEADINGS-READ, T-LEFT-EDGES and T-FIVE-SECOND pass, but T-SQUINT finds the seven category heads set at body size, so the groups in an 8,815px list do not hold their shape, and T-ANATOMY finds no in-page navigation for a 2,226-word reference.

findings.where: category heads Interactions to Design, tiles 1440-00 to 1440-07, 1440px
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the seven category h2s ("Interactions" at y=317 to "Design" at y=6313) are 16px, the same size as the body and the bold rule leads under them ("Keyboard works everywhere.", "Clear focus."). The later part heads ("Vercel-specific", "Integrate with Agents", "Join Vercel") are 24px. Under the squint the category heads read at the same weight as each rule lead.
findings.before: Category heads at 16px, part heads at 24px, rule leads at 16px bold.
findings.after: Set the category heads one step up (at least the 24px used for the part heads) or add space above them, so each category starts visibly.
findings.why: A reader scrolling to the Forms rules cannot find where Forms starts without reading every bold lead; the categories are the page's only grouping.

findings.evidence: The page has no nav landmark and no list of categories; the first screen goes from the intro paragraph straight into the 119 rule items (the start-line count gives 119 blocks at x=380). The category heads are anchor links, so targets exist, but nothing links to them. The page is 8,815px tall at 1440 and 14,211px at 375.
findings.before: A long single-column reference with no table of contents.
findings.after: Add a short list of the category anchors under the intro, or a sticky list in the empty left margin at 1440 (the column starts at x=360).
findings.why: Reference pages are read by jumping to a category; without a contents list the reader scrolls or uses find-in-page.

strengths: Every block starts on one of three related edges: x=360 for heads and paragraphs, x=380 for rule items, x=400 for nested examples. Nothing drifts.
The headings read alone outline the material: seven rule categories, then Vercel-specific preferences, then how to use the list with agents.
Each rule is one bold lead plus one sentence, so the skeleton itself says 'rule list' and every item carries one idea.
The first screen states what the page is and starts the first category inside the fold at every width; the 375 order matches 1440.
not_investigated: T-STOCK-ORDER and T-COMPOSITION-RUN: a Read page, where composition variety does not apply.
words_per_screen (292 words on screen 2) and page_words (2,226) are sweep findings; that density fits a reference list, so T-DENSITY-FIT passes.
One script chunk was blocked during capture (manifest network); copy buttons and similar interactions were not checked.
